correctness.rationale: For n>=2, token vertices split into hub h={a1,a2}, 2n cross vertices x_(r,i), and binomial(n,2) within-large-part vertices y_(ij). Explicit adjacency makes a dominating set equivalent to a partition of columns T/S/U (0/1/2 selected x vertices), a selected within-part edge set E containing the forced clique binom(T,2), and—when h omitted—positive E-degree at every vertex of T union S plus at least one selected cross vertex. These are necessary and sufficient, so hub-including sets factor as z sum binom(n,t) z^binom(t,2)(2z+z²)^(n-t)(1+z)^(M-binom(t,2)); hub-free sets are counted via inclusion-exclusion over uncovered T/S vertices, with t>=2 vs t<=1 branch. The minimal hub count occurs only t=1 or2, yielding n(n+3)2^(n-3) (including rational-written n2=5); direct equality case analysis of |D|=n-t+u+e proves hub-free minima only n2,3,4 with counts 4,15,24, so total minima 9,33,80, n(n+3)2^(n-3) thereafter and all contain hub from n>=5. No claim for higher tokens or other domination notions.

Counting by forced cliques and edge-incidence degree makes it nontrivial despite an earlier feasibility lemma.
